why: The widest honest value every reading on a page is photographed at (R-UI-23).
The capture gate used to paint a grey box over every reading, because a load
average is different on two runs and would leave the committed picture
permanently dirty. That kept the file clean and it hid the defect the pictures
exist to catch: a readout row is only ever as wrong as its *longest* value, and
the value that happens to be on the page during a capture is never the longest
one. `2000 kb/s` fits. `20000 kb/s`, which `schema/config.ts` allows, is what an
operator's page actually has to hold — and nothing in this repository had ever
drawn one.
So each field is given one value here and the gate renders that instead of a
mask. The picture is still identical on two runs, which is what the masking was
for, and it is now a picture of the hardest case rather than of the easiest.
**A page of specimens is not a board.** Every field is at its own widest, so
the lamp can read NOTHING beside a sentence about a path that is carrying
traffic. That is what the picture is for: it is not a portrait of one device
in one state, it is the layout under the hardest content each of its fields
can hold. The unmasked copy under `vendor/capture/` is the page as it really
was, taken before any of this is written.
**Honest means the value can actually arrive.** Every entry names where its
value comes from: a bound in `schema/config.ts`, the longest branch of the
function that composes the sentence, or the widest reading a real board has
produced. A value invented to be long would fail the gate on a defect the
console does not have, which costs the gate its credibility faster than
missing one.
**A field is named by the instrument it is drawn in and the caption beside**
**it** — `nrdb-ui-yonder-databar · UPLINK`. Not a DOM path and not a node id,
because this file has to be checkable against the page by a person. Rename a
caption and the specimen goes missing, loudly, which is the right failure: the
widest honest value for UPLINK is not automatically the widest honest value for
whatever it was renamed to.
`masked` is the other half, and it is what stops this file from being a list of
the easy ones. Every reading the gate finds is either specified here or listed
there with a reason; a reading that is neither fails the build and names the key
to add. An entry on either list that matches no reading on any page also fails —
the same rule `accepted-violations.json` is held to, for the same reason.
**No credential belongs in here (R-SEC-10).** These values are rendered into
pages that are screenshotted and committed. The receive line resolves a real
RTSP password on a real device, so the fixture carries a visibly fake one and
the specimen for a stream address carries no password at all.

nrdb-ui-yonder-databar · BOARD.why: displayFacts' `model`, verbatim from /proc/device-tree/model. The Compute Module's string is the longest of the boards this project is built for.

nrdb-ui-yonder-databar · UP FOR.why: formatUptime, which prints the largest two units only. Days is the largest unit it has and a board left flying a season is three digits of them.

nrdb-ui-yonder-databar · YONDER.why: the version out of package.json. A pre-release with build metadata is the longest semver this project can publish.

nrdb-ui-yonder-databar · SYSTEM.why: the OS version string, verbatim from /etc/os-release PRETTY_NAME on the distribution the installer targets.

nrdb-ui-yonder-databar · OPERATOR.why: the operator name ModemManager reports. 3GPP allows 24 characters of long alphanumeric name plus a service-provider suffix; this is a real one at that width.

nrdb-ui-yonder-databar · NETWORK.why: formatTechnology, which uppercases ModemManager's identifier. `5gnr` is the longest of the ones it reports.

nrdb-ui-yonder-databar · REGISTERED.why: the registration state, in ModemManager's own words. `searching` is the longest of home / roaming / searching / denied / idle.

nrdb-ui-yonder-databar · APN.why: an APN as carriers publish them. 3GPP allows 100 characters; this is the longest form actually issued — a full operator-scoped name.

nrdb-ui-yonder-databar · RSSI.why: the floor of the RSSI range a modem reports, which is the widest because it is the only three-digit one.

nrdb-ui-yonder-databar · RSRQ.why: the floor of the LTE RSRQ range (-3 to -19.5 dB), which is the widest value the field can carry.

nrdb-ui-yonder-databar · MTU.why: a jumbo frame. The link MTU is read from the interface and nothing caps it below this.

nrdb-ui-yonder-databar · COMPOSITION.why: R-CEL-03's answer, one word, and MBIM is the longer of the two modes this device chooses between.

nrdb-ui-yonder-databar · ADDRESS.why: the widest IPv4 address. The link address on Status and on the Cellular tab is the same field asked twice.

nrdb-ui-text.yonder-qualifier.value: Ethernet is carrying traffic, and nothing has stood down
nrdb-ui-text.yonder-qualifier.why: reachWhy's longest sentence, with the longest of PATH_WORDS' names (`ethernet`) raised by pathName.

nrdb-ui-text.value: The modem reported a failure: sim-pin-incorrect
nrdb-ui-text.why: modemSummary's longest branch (yonder-core/src/net/modem/state.ts), with the longest failure reason ModemManager gives. Drawn on the Interfaces tab and on the Cellular tab, which is why one specimen serves two widgets.

nrdb-ui-text · Address.why: the widest IPv4 address with its prefix length, which is the form NetworkManager reports.

nrdb-ui-text · Remote.why: messageFor's `label` (node-red-contrib-yonder-remote/src/state.ts). The longest of its seven phases.

nrdb-ui-text · Status.why: the same messageFor `label`, drawn again at the top of the ZeroTier tab.

nrdb-ui-text · Path.why: R-VPN-03's two words, in words rather than a boolean. `Relayed` is the longer.

nrdb-ui-text · Latency.why: messageFor's `${ms} ms`. Four digits is a relayed hop over a congested cellular uplink, and the widest worth reporting.

nrdb-ui-text · Network name.why: the name the mesh controller published. Nothing caps it, so this is the longest a controller has been configured with here.

nrdb-ui-text · Network.why: a ZeroTier network id, which is always sixteen hex characters.

nrdb-ui-text · Traffic.why: messageFor's `traffic`, at formatBytes' top tier (GB) with the one decimal it prints from MB up.

nrdb-ui-text · Throughput.why: messageFor's `throughput`, at formatRate's top tier (Gbps) with its one decimal. R-NET-10.

nrdb-ui-text · Last heard.why: formatLastHeard's longest branch. Minutes is where its digits and its unit are both widest.

nrdb-ui-table · Time.why: a clock, at the widest hour. Fixed width, so this is both the widest and the only honest value.

nrdb-ui-table · Time (UTC).why: the same clock on the Log page, under its own column title.

nrdb-ui-table · Level.why: the longest of the levels the daemon writes: info, warn, error.

nrdb-ui-table · What happened.value: network: a check of which way out is working did not finish in time; going on without it
nrdb-ui-table · What happened.why: the longest line the daemon actually writes to its journal, verbatim from net/watchdog.ts.

nrdb-ui-table.value: network: a check of which way out is working did not finish in time; going on without it
nrdb-ui-table.why: the same journal line in the Activity table's second column, whose title is deliberately empty.

nrdb-ui-table · Camera.why: a V4L2 card name, which the kernel caps at 32 characters plus the bus suffix v4l2-ctl prints after it.

nrdb-ui-table · Configured as.why: the camera's id in config.yaml. Nothing caps it, so this is the longest an operator writes by hand.

nrdb-ui-table · Identity.value: platform-fd500000.pcie-pci-0000:01:00.0-usb-0:1.3:1.0-video-index0 — an enumeration number; it may mean a different camera after a reboot
nrdb-ui-table · Identity.why: identityWords' longer branch, on the by-path name the bench board really answered. The schema permits 128 characters of device name; this is the widest one observed.

nrdb-ui-table · What it offers.value: formats: 10 · zoom: yes · focus: auto focus has it · exposure: aperture priority has it · whiteBalance: auto white balance has it · rotation: none · aim: advertised · recording: none · stills: none
nrdb-ui-table · What it offers.why: the capability summary with every key present, which is what a camera answering all of them composes to.

nrdb-ui-table · Device.why: the highest V4L2 device node the kernel enumerates, and so the widest this column carries.

nrdb-ui-table · Card.why: the same V4L2 card name, in the rejection table's own column.

nrdb-ui-table · Why.value: bcm2835-codec-decode is a hardware codec on this board, not a camera; it appears in the device list and answers nothing a camera would
nrdb-ui-table · Why.why: the longest rejection reason detectCameras composes, on the node a Raspberry Pi really offers.

nrdb-ui-yonder-databar · RUNNING.value: failed — the pipeline exited with code 1; gave up after 5 restarts
nrdb-ui-yonder-databar · RUNNING.why: runWords with the supervisor's longest reason: the exit branch plus the MAX_RESTARTS = 5 suffix it adds when it stops trying.

nrdb-ui-yonder-databar · PICTURE.why: cameraStrip's `width × height` at the schema's ceilings (width max 3840, height max 2160).

nrdb-ui-yonder-databar · RATE.why: cameraStrip's `framerate fps` at the schema's ceiling of 60.

nrdb-ui-yonder-databar · BITRATE.why: cameraStrip's `bitrate_kbps kb/s` at the schema's ceiling of 20000. This is the defect spec §10 lists second: 2000 fits and 20000 does not.

nrdb-ui-yonder-databar · UPLINK.why: cameraStrip's uplink: atIp(20000) × 8 outputs + atIp(4000) preview, at the schema's ceilings (outputs max 8, preview bitrate max 4000), in Mb/s to two places.

nrdb-ui-text · Before you press Start.value: this device cannot serve SRT yet: the output on port 8890 would listen with no password on it (R-VID-06). Remove it, or use an RTSP output, which carries this device's own credential
nrdb-ui-text · Before you press Start.why: cameraStrip's startCheck at refuse()'s longest branch, verbatim from video/pipeline.ts.

nrdb-ui-text · Camera.value: Forward observation camera, port side pod
nrdb-ui-text · Camera.why: the camera's name. `schema/config.ts` caps it at 48 characters and an operator types it, so the cap is the honest ceiling.

nrdb-ui-text · Identity.value: platform-fd500000.pcie-pci-0000:01:00.0-usb-0:1.3:1.0-video-index0 — an enumeration number; it may mean a different camera after a reboot
nrdb-ui-text · Identity.why: identityWords' longer branch again, on the Setup deck rather than in the Cameras table.

nrdb-ui-text · Encoder.why: cameraStrip's encoder line. The board's hardware element is the longer of the two probeEncoder returns.

nrdb-ui-yonder-gauge · CPU LOAD.why: A gauge draws the same number twice — once as text and once as a needle — and this gate can move only one of them. A specimen here would commit a picture of a needle at one value with another value written beside it, which is a worse record than a grey box. The gauges are the one instrument whose reading cannot be substituted from outside; a widest-value gauge has to be driven through the daemon.

nrdb-ui-yonder-gauge · CPU TEMP.why: As CPU LOAD: text and needle, and only the text can be written from here.

nrdb-ui-yonder-gauge · MEMORY.why: As CPU LOAD: text and needle, and only the text can be written from here.

nrdb-ui-yonder-gauge · SIGNAL.why: As CPU LOAD: text and needle, and only the text can be written from here.

nrdb-ui-yonder-gauge · QUALITY.why: As CPU LOAD: text and needle, and only the text can be written from here.

nrdb-ui-yonder-annunciator.yonder-live.y.why: The confirmation countdown. It has a widest honest value — the full window, at three digits — and writing it would put CHANGE PENDING on every page captured with nothing pending, which is the one thing about this annunciator a picture has to get right. The pending captures (status-pending, network-cellular-pending) exist to photograph the other state, and they are the reason a single specimen cannot be honest for both.

nrdb-ui-text · Host.why: Nothing composes a value for this field yet. The widget binds {{msg.payload}} straight from yonder-diag, which sends the daemon's whole reply object, so the field renders nothing until a probe runs and an object afterwards. A specimen would state a format this console does not have.

nrdb-ui-text · Replies.why: As Host: bound to the whole yonder-diag payload, with no composed value to be the widest of.

nrdb-ui-text · Round trip (ms).why: As Host: bound to the whole yonder-diag payload, with no composed value to be the widest of.

nrdb-ui-text · Probed.why: As Host: bound to the whole yonder-diag payload, with no composed value to be the widest of.
